title: Daytime radiative cooling material durability
bottleneck: Radiative cooling metamaterials can dump heat to space through the atmospheric transparency window, cooling below ambient with no energy input, but outdoor durability is poor: UV exposure yellows polymers, dust and soiling degrade the delicate optical structures, and moisture infiltration ruins performance. No formulation yet survives multi-year rooftop exposure while maintaining the precise emissivity spectrum the effect requires.
why_it_blocks: Passive cooling could cut air-conditioning energy — a fast-growing share of global electricity — with zero operating cost. Durability failures mean every demonstration degrades within months outdoors, so the technology cannot yet displace any installed cooling capacity.
current_state: Encapsulated photonic films and self-cleaning surface treatments have extended lifetimes in field trials, but the combination of UV stability, soiling resistance, and low cost in one manufacturable product is still missing.
